report.headline: Efficient, ball-dominant EuroLeague scorer projects to a near-average NBA usage role, with a shooting forecast that the model itself cannot beat a naive guess on

projection.text: Usage rate is projected to fall to 19.4% in the NBA, down from 25.7% in the EuroLeague, landing just below the NBA's minutes-weighted average of 20.1%, with an 80% interval of 13.8% to 25.1%. True shooting is projected at 59.0%, down from 67.1% in the EuroLeague and close to the NBA average of 58.1%, with an 80% interval of 52.8% to 65.3%.

risks.text: The projected 19.4% NBA usage rate sits inside an 80% interval running from 13.8% to 25.1%, a span of roughly two standard deviations of the league's usage spread (5.6%), so the model can rank this player among peers but cannot pin down an individual usage figure.

The 59.0% true shooting projection is not more accurate than simply guessing the league average, since both carry a 4.7% mean absolute error, so it should not be relied on to describe expected efficiency.
The source season is a modest sample of 874 minutes across 38 games at age 27, and the model behind this projection is fitted on only 61 prior EuroLeague-to-NBA transitions.

Only about 58% of a player's usage standing above the EuroLeague average is estimated to carry over to the NBA, versus 75.4% for true shooting, consistent with a shrinking offensive role in the new league.

strengths.text: Scored heavily and efficiently in the EuroLeague, averaging 20.638 points per 75 possessions on a 67.1% true shooting mark, +1.29 standard deviations above the EuroLeague average that season.
Carried a featured offensive role, with a 25.7% usage rate that stood +1.09 standard deviations above the EuroLeague average.
Combined scoring with playmaking, posting a 21.1% assist rate and 4.202 assists per 75 possessions.
Kept turnovers modest for the workload, at a 15.2% turnover rate alongside the high usage and assist figures.

uncertainty.text: The usage projection beats the trivial league-mean baseline (3.3% mean absolute error versus 4.3%), so it carries some signal, but the true-shooting model is exactly as accurate as the trivial baseline (4.7% versus 4.7%) and should not be treated as informative. Both estimates rest on only 61 historical EuroLeague-to-NBA transitions.
